title: Hybrid films loaded with 5-fluorouracil and Reglan for synergistic treatment of colon cancer via asynchronous dual-drug

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods section, drug description paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states 'Reglan is also called metoclopramide or Chloramphenicol; it is a white to light-yellow crystalline powder with the molecular formula C14H22ClN3O2. It is also known as 4-amino-5-chloro N-(2-diethylamine)-2-methoxybenzamide.' Chloramphenicol is an entirely different drug (a broad-spectrum antibiotic with molecular formula C11H12Cl2N2O5), unrelated to metoclopramide (an antiemetic/prokinetic agent). The molecular formula and chemical name given (C14H22ClN3O2, 4-amino-5-chloro-N-(2-diethylamino)-2-methoxybenzamide) correspond only to metoclopramide, not to chloramphenicol, creating an internal inconsistency: the text equates two chemically and pharmacologically distinct compounds under one name while only supplying the formula for one of them.

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods, 'drug loading efficiencies' subsection
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper calculates loading efficiency (LE) for 5-FU in particles S2/S3 via an extraction method (dissolving particles, precipitating polymer, and measuring 5-FU in the aqueous phase), but then states 'The LE (%) value of Reglan in the solid film was determined through an in vitro dissolution test.' Using a dissolution (release) test to determine total drug loading is methodologically inconsistent with the extraction-based approach used for 5-FU, since dissolution testing measures time-dependent release rather than total incorporated drug content, and no justification or correction factor is provided for assuming complete recovery at test endpoint equals total loading efficiency.
